alt_text: 25 accepted dates are shown as three-stage Mall Skate, Walk, and PT Skate profiles. Metric-specific directions remain mixed; canonical same-day CSS is shown when materialized, and reciprocal CSS rows are omitted from the default view.
finding: The repeated sequence separates a controlled rolling comparator, a short ballistic walking challenge, and continued post-walk PT mobility without claiming that PT is lower on every measure.
functional_meaning: The stage order shows why PT should be interpreted as functional continuation after walking rather than as a universally lower-burden condition.
interpretation: The repeated protocol shows consistent stage structure with metric-specific PT movement toward Mall, away from Mall, or unchanged; no universal return claim is made.
limitation: The fixed stage order may include order, duration, and environment effects; repeated observations are from one individual.
limitations: Wearables estimate physiologic, autonomic, MSK, movement, impact, and transport burden. They do not directly measure pain. Results are N-of-1 evidence, not clinical proof, diagnosis, causation, universal proof, or legal proof.
long_description: The repeated protocol shows consistent stage structure with metric-specific PT movement toward Mall, away from Mall, or unchanged; no universal return claim is made. CSS connectors show three unique stage pairs when persisted canonical same-day CSS is available; an unavailable date is explicit, and reciprocal or identity rows are audit-only. Return direction is descriptive, not Cohort Similarity Score. Wearables estimate physiologic, autonomic, MSK, movement, impact, and transport burden. They do not directly measure pain. Results are N-of-1 evidence, not clinical proof, diagnosis, causation, universal proof, or legal proof.
